facts.text: The opening credits list 'Other Titles We Didn't Use,' including 'Crouching Tiger, Hidden .357,' 'Teen Sewer Tramps' and 'Used Love Dolls: We Got 'Em Cheap.'
Film Threat's Steve Anderson wrote that the movie has only three moods: comic, disgusting and pandering. He called it a thrill ride for every fifteen-year-old boy.
Director Kevin Campbell joked he wanted this film to deliver all the T&A hijinks and nudity that the cheerleader hit Bring It On (2001) should have had.
Film Threat's Eric Campos called this the 'real sequel' to Revenge of the Nerds (1984). That hit grossed about $40.9M on a $6-8M budget; critics panned it then, but it became a cult favorite.
Kevin Campbell's earlier credits were VHS how-to tapes like Video Workbench: How to Build WWII Aircraft and Basic Modeling. Model-kit tutorials to ninja cheerleaders is quite a leap.
The Happy Valley High Hamsters are played by Englewood High School in Colorado, whose real mascot is the Pirate. The school dates to 1913; its current building opened with the class of 1954.
The film was shot at Englewood High School, so the Happy Valley High Hamsters were played by a real school's hallways.
The film was accepted to the 8th annual San Antonio Underground Film Festival (June 14-16, 2002). Campbell submitted it for its 'alternative, avant-garde nature,' Film Threat reported.
Jeff Nicholson, who plays teacher Stephen, drew the surreal graphic novel Through the Habitrails, first serialized in Stephen Bissette's Taboo. He has six Eisner Award nominations.
Film Threat's Eric Campos called it a 'real sequel' to Revenge of the Nerds and 'one of the craziest T&A comedies ever,' praising Kevin Campbell as 'a comic mastermind.'
Reviews split hard. Film Threat gave it four stars, while The Encyclopedia of Underground Movies found it more gory than funny.
Kira Reed (Fantasy Girl) later became a Playboy TV regular. Her show 69 Sexy Things 2 Do Before You Die was called Christie Hefner's favorite new show on the channel.
Film Threat's Eric Campos said director Kevin Campbell captures the feel of cheesy 1980s sex comedies and adds Troma-style lunacy. He called the result 'an ultimate party movie!'
Film Threat's Eric Campos noted Kira Reed, who plays Fantasy Girl, was a familiar face from late-night Skinemax films, and she appears in the nerds' fantasy sequences.
Fantasy Girl Kira Reed later moved to producing. She won Daytime Emmys as a producer in 2016 and 2017 on the web drama The Bay, and she was nominated for acting on it in 2018.
Jeff Nicholson, who plays Stephen, stopped drawing comics around 2005. He spent about 20 years at a utility company doing GIS work, retired at 55, and later revived his Ultra Klutz series.
Don't confuse it with Ninja Cheerleaders, the 2008 comedy starring George Takei. Cheerleader Ninjas came out about six years earlier.
The film's reference list also includes Barb Wire (1996), Mork & Mindy (1978), Star Trek: The Next Generation and Return of the Jedi.
The film name-checks Star Wars, Star Trek, The Exorcist, Top Gun, Highlander, Back to the Future and The X-Files, and spoofs Mighty Morphin Power Rangers.
Bands About Movies reviewed it in 2023 and said it 'sets out to be bad and overdelivers.' It also noted that Kira Reed supplies nearly all of the film's nudity.
Jeff Nicholson, who plays teacher Stephen, is also a cartoonist. He created the comic book Ultra Klutz, according to Bands About Movies.
Englewood High School, the film's real location, moved into a new 239,000-square-foot campus dedicated February 7, 2015. It now serves about 1,250 students.
Director Kevin Campbell returned to the internet-horror theme two decades later with the slasher Back Slash, according to Bands About Movies.
The uncredited topless body double in the catfight also doubled for head cheerleader Angela (Angela Brubaker). She appears in the film's lesbian dream sequence too.
Stay for the credits. The audio is credited to 'Deaf Dorkelston' and the fart noises to 'T.P. Brownpipe.' 'Dave the Sword-Clanging Guy' handles the sword effects.
The last credit thanks viewers 'so bored as to actually sit through all these credits,' and tells them never to let anyone ask them to pull their finger.
The credits show Kira Reed was one of the topless body doubles in the catfight, which is why the cheerleaders' blouses are intact again afterward.
